_comment: Quantitative comparison anchors for the maximal instep (laces) drive, keyed where possible to kick_metrics metric families. IMPORTANT unit conventions when comparing to our table: knee_angle and hip_angle are INTERIOR angles where 180 = fully straight, so a source reporting '55 deg of knee flexion at contact' corresponds to about 125 in our units; trunk_lean is signed positive TOWARD the target, so the skilled backward lean is negative. `confidence` grades the evidence, not the precision: 'established' = multiple independent studies agree, 'probable' = consistent but thinner, 'contested' = the literature genuinely disagrees, 'single-study' = one source only. Populations are mostly skilled ADULTS; youth rows are marked and should anchor youth feedback instead.

referenceValues.value: roughly 120-140 interior (40-60 deg of flexion) — the knee is NOT straight at contact; full extension arrives during follow-through
referenceValues.source: Alcock et al. 2012 (55.6+/-6.6 deg flexion); Cordeiro et al. (55.0+/-7.5); Navandar et al. 2018 (43+/-11 male dominant)

referenceValues.value: deepest fold roughly 60-90 interior (90-120 deg of flexion), reached at about 64% of the kick cycle
referenceValues.source: Navandar et al. 2018 (118+/-8 deg flexion male dominant, 112+/-11 female); Cordeiro (93.3+/-5.2); Langhout et al. 2015 (timing)

referenceValues.value: from about 10-30 deg of hip extension at end of backswing, through 28-35 deg of flexion at contact, to 85-97 deg of flexion at end of follow-through
referenceValues.source: Navandar et al. 2018 (-13+/-8 backswing, 28+/-9 contact, 97+/-16 follow-through); Alcock et al. 2012 (35.5+/-7.8 at impact)

referenceValues.value: roughly 500-630 deg/s, peaking BEFORE the shank and decelerating toward zero at impact
referenceValues.source: Huang 1982; Lees & Nolan 1998 (516-573 deg/s segment peak); Navandar 2018 (11+/-1 rad/s hip flexion)

referenceValues.value: roughly 1600-2500 deg/s — two to three times the thigh's peak; the largest angular velocity in the body
referenceValues.source: Dorge et al. 1999 (1891 deg/s); Navandar 2018 (1834 male dominant, 1604 female); Nunome 2002 (860-1720)

referenceValues.value: true in skilled kickers: peak angular velocity is reached first by the thigh, then the shank, then the foot; at impact thigh velocity is near zero while the shank is at peak
referenceValues.source: Kellis & Katis 2007 (review); Huang 1982; Lees et al. 2010

referenceValues.value: roughly 15-20 m/s at the ankle/foot; rank order hip < knee < ankle < foot demonstrates velocity amplification
referenceValues.source: Alcock et al. 2012 (ankle 15.54+/-0.96, 5th metatarsal 17.70+/-1.92 m/s); Palucci Vieira 2021 (foot CoM 20.35+/-0.94)

referenceValues.value: adult range 18-35 m/s; elite males 26-32, elite females 21-25; ball travels roughly 1.4x foot speed
referenceValues.source: Kellis & Katis 2007; Barfield 2002 (male dominant 25.3+/-1.51, female 21.5+/-2.44 m/s); Palucci Vieira 2021 (ratio 1.47+/-0.06)

referenceValues.value: rises roughly linearly and about doubles across youth: U9 48.5, U11 57.9, U13 66.7, U15 76.9, U17 81.4, U20 98.7 km/h (3D kinematics; radar-behind-goal values run much higher)
referenceValues.source: Palucci Vieira et al., youth cross-sectional series; Rada et al. 2019 (radar method contrast)

referenceValues.value: impact quality improves with age independently of foot speed: U9 0.99, U13 1.10, U15 1.18, U20 1.26
referenceValues.source: Palucci Vieira et al., youth cross-sectional series

referenceValues.value: support foot level with or slightly AHEAD of ball centre — about 0.10 m ahead in the fore-aft axis
referenceValues.source: Alcock et al. 2012 (support heel to ball centre y = 0.10+/-0.07 m); Ou, Lei & Cheng 2023

referenceValues.metric: plant foot lateral offset (not directly measured sagittally)
referenceValues.value: CONTESTED: elite adults measure 0.27-0.37 m to the side, while the classic coaching prescription is 15-20 cm and one youth study found CLOSER placement predicted faster kicks (14.1+/-7.4 cm)
referenceValues.source: Alcock 2012 (0.33+/-0.07 m); Hay 1993 textbook (5-28 cm); Kapidzic et al. (youth, beta = -0.269); Ou et al. 2023

referenceValues.value: does NOT change with age (U9 0.33, U13 0.34, U20 0.35 m) — a pure technique variable, not a maturation one, so it is fair to coach at any age
referenceValues.source: Palucci Vieira et al., youth cross-sectional series

referenceValues.value: roughly 138 interior (about 42 deg of flexion), from about 154 interior (26 deg) at touchdown; extension begins just before contact
referenceValues.source: Lees et al. 2009

referenceValues.value: a MORE extended, stiffer support leg is associated with faster kicking-foot speed and better accuracy (+1.2 m/s ball speed when deliberately increased)
referenceValues.source: support-leg intervention study (25.1 -> 26.3 m/s; support-knee flexion 38 vs 45 deg)

referenceValues.value: skilled kickers lean BACKWARD 12-18 deg (NEGATIVE in our sign convention) and laterally 10-16 deg toward the non-kicking side; more backward lean produces a higher launch angle (13 deg low vs 17 deg high trajectory)
referenceValues.source: Lees & Nolan 2002 in Lees et al. 2010; Prassas, Terauds & Nathan 1990; Alcock 2012 (elite women -5.8+/-8.3)

referenceValues.value: the pelvis progressively squares to the target, closing from about 21 deg open at support-foot touchdown to about 6 deg at ball contact; total retraction-to-protraction range 30-36 deg
referenceValues.source: Navandar et al. (21.5 -> 6 deg); Lees et al. 2010 (30-36 deg range)

referenceValues.metric: hip-shoulder separation (tension arc; not directly measured)
referenceValues.value: 38-42 deg in maximal kicks vs 6-12 deg in submaximal — the clearest maximal-vs-submaximal discriminator in the upper body
referenceValues.source: Lees & Nolan, reported in Lees et al. 2010

referenceValues.value: non-kicking-side shoulder abducted roughly 48 deg at impact; the arm travels through 158 deg of horizontal extension in the kick stride vs 63 deg in a running stride
referenceValues.source: Alcock et al. 2012 (-48.2+/-11.7 deg); Lees et al. 2010 (stride ROM comparison)

referenceValues.value: 30-45 deg maximises ball speed and beats a straight approach by 3-7.5%; skilled players self-select about 43 deg, though elite 3D studies have measured as low as 18 deg
referenceValues.source: Isokawa & Lees 1988; Kellis et al.; Egan 2007 (43 deg); Alcock 2012 (18.0+/-7.3 deg)

referenceValues.value: elite adults 1.55-1.60 m; in youth it is the most consistently ball-speed-related approach variable (r rises from .36 at U9 to .79 at U15) and grows U9 1.09 -> U20 1.60 m
referenceValues.source: Alcock 2012 (1.55+/-0.14 m); Langhout et al. (1.60 m); Palucci Vieira youth series

referenceValues.value: modest 2.8-3.7 m/s over 2-4 steps (about 3.3 m/s typical); each player has an individual optimum and running faster than it REDUCES ball speed
referenceValues.source: Augustus, Hudson & Smith 2021; Lees et al. 2010

referenceValues.value: maximum ball velocity comes from striking 20-40 mm BELOW the ball's centre of mass with zero horizontal offset; contact lasts 9-10 ms
referenceValues.source: impact-modelling literature; contact duration 9.0+/-0.4 ms

referenceValues.value: about 25% of the whole kick (0.150+/-0.038 s), ending with the kicking hip at 85-97 deg flexion and the knee near-extended
referenceValues.source: Langhout et al. 2015/2016; Navandar et al. 2018

referenceValues.value: an accuracy constraint costs roughly 15% of maximal ball speed in adults (most accurate kicks at about 85% of max), but in YOUTH the trade-off is only partial — kicking harder does not generally cost placement accuracy
referenceValues.source: van den Tillaar (adults); Palucci Vieira youth series (r between ball velocity and radial error negative or absent at every youth age)
